sentences.text: 3. Appellant - Rinku has been convicted and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of ten years along with a fine of Rs.25,000/- for the offence under Section 376(2)(i) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short, "IPC"); he has been convicted and sentenced to undergo imprisonment for a period of two years along with a fine of Rs.5,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 506 IPC, and, he has been further convicted and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of ten years along with a fine of Rs.20,000/- for the offence under Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 vide judgment and order dated 04.02.2021, passed by learned Additional District and Sessions Judge/ Special Judge (POCSO), Haridwar in Special Sessions Trial No.48 of 2018, "State vs. Rinku".

entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge/ Special Judge (POCSO), Haridwar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: All the sentences have been directed to run concurrently.

4. Heard Mr. Arvind Vashistha, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Rachit Manglik, learned counsel holding brief of Mr. Vivek Pathak, learned counsel for the appellant, Mr. Rakesh Negi,
learned Brief Holder for the State and Mr. Pankaj Sanwal, learned counsel holding brief of Mr. Deep Chandra Joshi, learned counsel for the victim.
5.
Mr. Arvind Vashistha, learned Senior Advocate contended that the appellant is a permanent resident of District Haridwar, therefore, there is no chance of his absconding.
He was on bail during the trial and the conditions of bail were neither violated nor misused by him, and, he has spent more than four years in judicial custody.
6. Mr. Rakesh Negi, learned Brief Holder and Mr. Pankaj Sanwal, learned counsel appearing for the victim have opposed the bail application.
They further submitted that if the appellant is released on bail, then it would be appropriate to impose stringent conditions on the appellant in the bail order.

7. Having considered the submissions of learned counsel for both the parties, and in the facts and circumstances of this case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is inclined to grant bail to the appellant provided he submits a personal bond of Rs.30,000/- and two reliable sureties of the same amount to the satisfaction of the trial court.

He is further directed to observe the following condition:-
"He (appellant) shall not contact, nor visit, nor offer any inducement, threat or promise to the victim or informant or to any of the prosecution witnesses".
8.
In case of breach of the said condition, the respondents shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application.
9. Third Bail Application (IA No.07 of 2024) stands disposed of accordingly.

__ ALOK KUMAR VERMA, J.
Dt: 12th July, 2024 Pant/
